# NVDA Technical Analysis Report (as of 2026-11-16)

## 1. Summary

NVDA is in a sharp, high-volume breakdown. The verified close on 2026-11-16 was **156.14**, down from **239.24** on 2026-10-06. That is **-83.10 points, about -34.7%**, in 28 trading sessions. Every indicator selected here confirms the downtrend. Momentum is deeply oversold, but no indicator shows a reversal signal yet.

The tools give no information on the cause of the move, so none is assumed. Everything below is technical.

**Data integrity:** The verified snapshot and the `get_indicators` outputs agree on every shared value (10 EMA, 50 SMA, 200 SMA, RSI, lower Bollinger band, MACD, ATR). VWMA (176.60) is not in the snapshot. It comes only from `get_indicators`, so treat it as unverified by the snapshot. I found no discrepancies. The MACD signal, histogram, Bollinger middle and upper bands appear only in the snapshot.

## 2. Indicators selected and why

I chose eight indicators that cover different dimensions with little overlap:

| Dimension | Indicator | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Short-term trend | close_10_ema | Fast read on momentum shifts and mean-reversion distance |
| Medium-term trend | close_50_sma | Trend direction and overhead reference |
| Long-term trend | close_200_sma | Strategic regime benchmark |
| Momentum/trend change | macd (with macds and macdh from the snapshot) | Direction and acceleration of the move |
| Overbought/oversold | rsi | Extreme-reading and divergence check |
| Volatility/range | boll_lb (with boll and boll_ub from the snapshot) | Statistical extreme and band context |
| Risk sizing | atr | Stop distance and position sizing in a high-volatility regime |
| Volume confirmation | vwma | Whether volume supports price direction |

## 3. Price action and volume

The decline came in stages, and volume expanded sharply during the later stages.

- **Early weakness (Oct 8 – Nov 4):** Price slid from 230.48 to 200.13 on mostly ordinary volume (about 70–127M), apart from 168.4M on Oct 30.
- **Nov 5:** Close 181.60 (-18.53, about -9.3% from 200.13) on **306.1M** shares. The day opened with a gap down (open 196.07 versus the prior close of 200.13).
- **Nov 9:** Opened 173.07 against a prior close of 186.64, closed 178.67, on **462.7M**.
- **Nov 10:** Close 168.89 on **429.3M**.
- **Nov 12:** The largest-volume day in the six-month dataset at **747.7M**. It opened 151.01 (versus a prior close of 173.73), hit a low of **148.80**, and closed 166.19. That is a 18.34-point range, about 1.9 times the current ATR. The close was about 17.4 points off the low, which shows heavy two-way trading. It did not hold as a reversal, because the next two sessions closed lower.
- **Nov 13:** Close 162.85 on 363.8M.
- **Nov 16:** Open 159.00, high 163.00, low 155.01, close 156.14, on 326.6M.

**Observations:**
- Volume has stayed well above the roughly 75–200M range seen through most of the prior six months in each of the last seven sessions. A volume-driven selloff like this is usually repricing, not noise.
- Only two sessions since Nov 5 closed higher (Nov 6 at 186.64 and Nov 11 at 173.73). Both rallies faded immediately.
- The Nov 12 low (148.80) is **below** the current lower Bollinger band (152.62). The Nov 16 low (155.01) did not retest it.
- **Unfilled gaps above price**, taken from the OHLC data:
  - 167.14–170.77 (Nov 11 low versus Nov 12 high)
  - 179.92–185.22 (Nov 6 low versus Nov 9 high)
  - 196.25–199.68 (Nov 4 low versus Nov 5 high)

  These are untested reference zones. This dataset does not show whether they will act as resistance.
- **No prior support within the dataset:** The pre-selloff six-month low was about 189.59 (Jun 29 intraday), and price is now far below it. The dataset starts 2026-05-18, so there are no historical price references below 148.80.

## 4. Trend indicators

| Indicator | Value | Price vs. level |
|---|---:|---|
| close_10_ema | 176.12 | Price about 20.0 below (~11.4% under) |
| VWMA (20-day per tool default; unverified by snapshot) | 176.60 | Price about 20.5 below |
| close_50_sma | 213.15 | Price about 57.0 below |
| close_200_sma | 203.75 | Price about 47.6 below (~23.4%) |
| Bollinger middle (20 SMA) | 195.64 | Price about 39.5 below |

- **10 EMA is falling fast.** It went from 223.01 (Oct 19) to 176.12, and fell 4.44 points in the last session alone (180.56 to 176.12). Any rebound toward it will meet a lower level each day.
- **50 SMA is rolling over.** It slipped from about 222.8 (Oct 19) to 213.15, with the pace of decline picking up in November.
- **200 SMA is flat** at about 203.7–204.4 throughout the window. The long-term average has not yet turned down.
- **The 50/200 gap is narrowing.** The 50 SMA is still above the 200 SMA, but the gap has shrunk from about 20.0 points (Oct 19: 222.83 vs 202.81) to about **9.4 points** (213.15 vs 203.75). If the 50 SMA keeps falling while the 200 SMA stays flat, a bearish cross (death cross) could form. I cannot say when from this data. Treat it as a watch item, since it is a lagging signal.
- **VWMA is almost identical to the 10 EMA** (176.60 vs 176.12), and both sit well above price. Volume-weighted price is therefore not diverging from the unweighted trend. Heavy volume is occurring on down moves, which confirms the direction.

## 5. Momentum

- **MACD:** -15.37, signal -11.16, histogram **-4.22**. The MACD line has fallen almost every session since Oct 27 (-2.58 to -15.37). The histogram is negative and, with the MACD line accelerating down, momentum is still increasing to the downside. There is no crossover or histogram contraction yet.
- **RSI:** **22.72**, the lowest reading in the 30-day window. Recent readings: 25.40 (Nov 5), 30.77 (Nov 6), 27.41 (Nov 9), 23.95 (Nov 10), 28.74 (Nov 11), 25.99 (Nov 12), 24.86 (Nov 13), 22.72 (Nov 16). RSI has been at or near oversold since Nov 5.
- **No bullish divergence.** Price made new closing lows (156.14) and RSI also made a new low (22.72), so they are confirming each other. RSI below 30 can persist in strong downtrends, and a reading below 30 alone is not a buy signal.

## 6. Volatility and risk

- **Bollinger Bands:** lower 152.62, middle 195.64, upper 238.66. Price (156.14) is only 3.52 points above the lower band, and the band keeps dropping (213.99 on Oct 19 to 152.62). Price is hugging the band, as it does in strong trends. Closes outside the lower band have not occurred in the last six sessions' closes. The Nov 12 intraday low did break below it.
- **ATR:** 9.84, up from 5.93 on Oct 19 (about +66%). That is about **6.3% of price** per day on average. Volatility has regime-shifted, so position sizes and stops based on October volatility are too tight.
- **Illustrative stop distances** (not a recommendation): 1.5–2x ATR is about 14.8–19.7 points, or roughly 136.5–141.4 from 156.14. The Nov 12 range alone was 18.34 points. ATR is a lagging measure, and gaps (Nov 5, Nov 9, Nov 12) can skip stops entirely.

## 7. Scenarios to monitor

**Continuation lower**
- A close below the lower band (152.62) or a breach of the Nov 12 low (148.80) would extend the move into a price area with no reference in this dataset.
- MACD histogram widening further and RSI making new lows would add confirmation.
- A 50/200 SMA cross would signal that the longer-term trend is following.

**Relief bounce or stabilization**
Signs to look for (none present yet):
- RSI turning up from oversold, ideally forming a higher low than 22.72 while price holds above 148.80
- MACD histogram contracting (less negative) for several sessions
- A volume decline on down days, indicating selling exhaustion
- Recent closing levels of 162.85 (Nov 13) and 166.19 (Nov 12), then the 167.14–170.77 gap, are the first overhead references.
- 10 EMA / VWMA near 176 would be the next, though the level is falling daily.
- The 50 SMA (213.15) and 200 SMA (203.75) are far overhead, about 37% and 30% above the current price respectively. A recovery to them would take a large move.

## 8. Bottom line

- **Trend:** Strongly bearish on every timeframe in the data. Price is below all moving averages and VWMA, and the 10 EMA and 50 SMA are declining.
- **Momentum:** Negative and still accelerating (MACD histogram -4.22). RSI is extremely oversold (22.72) without divergence.
- **Volatility:** Elevated and rising (ATR 9.84, about 6.3% of price). Price sits near the lower Bollinger band.
- **Volume:** Heavy, with seven consecutive sessions far above the earlier norm, including 747.7M on Nov 12. The sellers are active, and the volume does not yet show exhaustion.
- **For the deciding agent:** This setup favors caution about catching a counter-trend bounce before there are confirmed momentum changes. Any exposure should be sized for 6%-per-day average swings and gap risk. The case for a bounce rests on oversold extremes alone, with nothing else confirming yet. The case for further downside has trend, momentum and volume all aligned.
- **Limitations:** These tools show no news, fundamentals or catalysts. Each indicator window is only 30 days. Price-level observations are derived from the six-month OHLC data and have not been tested as support or resistance.

Risks: governance and leadership uncertainty (possible board shake-up or CEO change); possible AI capex forecast cuts if the SemiAnalysis revision is accurate; AI-sector correlation and concentration (Nov 5 drop); rumor and misinformation, including audit/fraud talk, which adds noise and volatility.

## 3. Your Q2 earnings-quality rebuttal compares the wrong lines

You said Q2 net income ($59.7B) was below operating income ($63.7B), so earnings are "operationally driven." Operating income is **pre-tax** and net income is after tax. Net income is 93.7% of pre-tax operating income, which leaves only a 6.3% drag from tax and everything else.

- Your "$70B six-month FCF" is front-loaded by Q1. The trend is the signal, and it points the wrong way.

## 5. The balance sheet is changing

Noncurrent liabilities went from about **$20B to $48B in one quarter**, and total liabilities rose $27B. Vendor debt/equity implies roughly $39B of debt. Borrowing while cash conversion falls doesn't fit a "capital-light, self-funding" story. If the liabilities are long-term purchase commitments, they become a problem if demand slows. You said you're "not dismissing it," but your thesis is silent on what it means.

## 8. Insiders and governance

## 9. Macro offers no help

Polymarket pricing of 98% for no cuts in 2026 means **no multiple-expansion tailwind** for a stock with a beta of 2.25. A calm backdrop isn't a catalyst.

## Where I concede

- Fundamentals reported through July are excellent. Revenue is up 106%, and margins and operating leverage are real.
- Much bad news may already be priced in, and a strong print could squeeze bearish positioning.
- The four-minute StockTwits sample is weak, so I'm not leaning on it.
- Resolving the 156.14 price did settle that the multiples are live.

## Conclusion

Your thesis is "excellent trailing numbers at a low multiple." The data shows trailing numbers with growing strain: cash conversion at about 40%, assets outrunning revenue, liabilities up $27B in a quarter, and EPS padded by non-operating items. It also shows a **forward EPS target 60% above run-rate**, a possibly lower capex ceiling, no insider buying, and a technical breakdown still confirming on volume. Your "scale in with a stop under one ATR" plan buys into a binary earnings event with unknown cause, an unknown date and unresolved cash questions.

- OCF recovers toward net income, and the source of the $28B liability jump is benign.
- Guidance supports the $15.84 forward EPS without relying on non-operating gains.

Until then, risk is skewed to the downside, and the burden of proof sits with buyers of a falling knife.
